Vinogradova Cortical spreading depolarization (SD), a slow-propagating wave of transient cellular depolarization, reliably occurs after acute brain injury but usually remains undetected. Focal brain injury is known to produce a network-level dysfunction that changes the strength and direction of connectivity far beyond lesion site (connectional diaschisis) that can underlie post-injury neurological dysfunction. We suggested that injury-induced SD could contribute to connectional diaschisis and studied the effects of SD on functional and effective connectivity in neural networks supporting cognitive and sensory functions. Electrographic recordings of cortical activity were obtained in freely behaving rats immediately after focal micro-injury of the frontal cortex. The injury-induced SD propagated over the cortex of the ipsilesional hemisphere but never invaded the contralesional cortex. Strength and direction of connectivity were estimated using non-directional (mutual information function) and directional (transfer entropy) measures calculated for recordings from the retrosplenial (a key hub of the default-mode network) and somatosensory cortex. Mutual information analysis showed initial hypercoupling within the injured hemisphere (during SD) followed by longer interhemispheric decoupling (after SD termination). During post-SD hypoconnectivity, influence of the uninjured cortex on the injured one increased in both cortical regions. The retrosplenial cortex, component of the default-mode network, showed strong interhemispheric coupling during the baseline period and complex changes in connectivity after SD. Therefore, SD arising in the injured cortex disturbs long-range connectivity in distant cortical regions and causes widespread network alterations involving the default-mode network. Given the key role of the network in cognition, connectivity changes produced by injury-induced SD could contribute to the mechanisms of cognitive deficit after brain injury.
n2c2b8059fca3: Background Literacy is an important social determinant of health. Failure to develop emergent literacy skills before kindergarten is a risk factor for academic failure, poverty, incarceration, and early death. Reading comprehension depends on both language comprehension and alphabetic decoding skills. The Home Literacy Environment literature tends to focus on reading aloud to develop oral language but less is known about letter-themed tools. Design Our hypothesis was that letter-themed toys and books would be acceptable to all families but that lower socio-economic status (SES) households would be less likely to have them. Using methods of Community Based Participatory Research, 3 caregivers with young children living in the City of Rochester, NY, completed IRB training and provided cultural context for decisions throughout this study. We surveyed a convenience sample of 156 caregivers at 10 community events. We showed a poster with pictures of alphabet-themed toys and asked caregivers to count how many they had in the home. ZIP code was used as a proxy for SES. Results We surveyed 156 caregivers, excluding 13 responses because of missing information. Of the 143 remaining, 139 (97.2%) thought it was important that a child know most of the alphabet letters before kindergarten. 1 in 4 of our respondents didn’t have a single literacy toy in their home and an additional 1 in 6 had only one. We calculated a p value of 0.0004 for the hypothesis that there is a difference by SES in the number of these items in the home. Conclusions Our results are consistent with the hypothesis that joyful letter-themed tools are acceptable to parents in general but that low-SES households are less likely to have them. Closing the gap in early alphabet exposure could contribute to reducing inequities in school success and lifelong health.
nea3c72c92f5e: As renewable energy penetration continues to increase, accurate ultra-short-term solar irradiance forecasting is essential for improving energy utilization and supporting power system operation. However, irradiance variations are jointly influenced by historical trends and rapid cloud changes, making traditional single-modal methods insufficient for capturing complex dynamics under varying weather conditions. This paper proposes a multimodal solar irradiance forecasting framework based on the collaborative representation of sky cloud images and numerical sequences. The framework introduces a heterogeneous modal state encoding mechanism and a state-aware adaptive selective attention fusion mechanism to enhance interactions between visual weather information and historical physical patterns. Specifically, the numerical modality captures irradiance trends and temporal correlations through dependency modeling, while the image modality extracts cloud structures and evolution features through spatiotemporal representation. The proposed fusion mechanism dynamically adjusts modality contributions according to forecasting conditions, enabling effective integration of complementary information. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms benchmark models in forecasting accuracy and robustness, validating the effectiveness of combining visual cloud information with numerical evolution patterns for ultra-short-term solar irradiance forecasting.
n9bc52ebdc152: Introduction Multiple long-term conditions (MLTC) or multimorbidity are becoming increasingly common in low- and middle-income countries, such as India, placing demands on constrained primary healthcare systems that are still predominantly organised around acute care and single-condition management. Weak referral, counter-referral, and follow-up processes contribute to fragmented care and poor continuity for people living with MLTC. This programme of work aims to develop an integrated referral and follow-up model for people with MLTC who seek care in the primary healthcare system in India. Methods This sequential, multistage mixed-methods research programme will be conducted in three interlinked phases. First, a systematic review of global literature will be conducted, which will synthesise evidence on referral and follow-up models or systems for providing MLTC care. Second, a convergent mixed-methods assessment will be undertaken in Jodhpur district, Rajasthan, including facility assessments of Primary Health Centres and linked referral facilities, a cross-sectional survey of adults with MLTC, and in-depth interviews with patients, caregivers, healthcare providers, and policymakers. Quantitative data will be analysed using descriptive and inferential statistics, while qualitative data will be analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Third, an integrated referral and follow-up model, SYNC-RF (SYstem for Navigation, Coordination, Referral, and Follow-up), will be developed based on the triangulated evidence and refined through expert consultation to ensure feasibility and contextual relevance. Conclusion The study will generate context-specific evidence on gaps, barriers, and enabling factors affecting referral and follow-up for MLTC care. The integrated model developed through this research is expected to strengthen continuity of care, improve coordination across various levels of the health system, and improve health outcomes for those living with MLTC.
ne9ed5e9306b3: Background Fever with neutropenia (FN) is a common complication of cancer therapy associated with significant morbidity, mortality, and resource use. Clinicians currently may access multiple Clinical Practice Guidelines (CPG) for FN in children to guide decision-making, however variation in content could impact care globally. We performed a systematic review and content analysis of CPG to assess the impact of databases searched and publication language on the quantity, quality, and content of recommendations identified for pediatric FN. Methods We conducted a systematic search of PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science databases to identify evidence-based CPG published in the last 10 years addressing FN in children. We categorized CPG by language, extracted recommendations, characterized recommendation type (diagnostic, prognostic, or treatment), direction, and agreement with a recently developed international guideline. Methodological quality was assessed using the AGREE-II instrument and comparison between English and non-English CPG was performed using the Mann-Whitney U test. Comparisons of recommendation type (treatment, prognosis, diagnosis) and agreement with a reference guideline were assessed using the Chi-square test. Results Fourteen CPG met inclusion criteria. Ten were published in English and four in non-English languages. There was no significant difference in methodological quality between language categories across AGREE-II domains except for scope and purpose (95.2% versus 90.5%; p = 0.036). Each database contained one unique guideline and only 36% (5/14) of the CPG were indexed in three databases. Percentage agreement between recommendations covered by 14 CPG and the reference CPG ranged between 33% and 100%. Conclusions Using pediatric FN as an index topic, we found that language or database restrictions limit the quantity and content of recommendations. Since CPG have variable methodological quality regardless of source, clinicians should design appropriate search strategies based on context. We recommend a broad search strategy when healthcare context or disease prevalence differs across settings.
nae975bba2631: The persistent yield gap remains a major challenge in organic agriculture despite its increasing importance for sustainable food production. The present study compared the performance of 80 diverse rice genotypes (62 landraces and 18 modern varieties) under two contrasting production systems (organic and conventional). The experiment was conducted during the Kharif seasons of 2023 and 2024 using an alpha lattice design (8 × 10) with three replications. Agro-morphological and yield-related traits were analysed through pooled mixed-model analysis of variance (ANOVA), genetic variability parameters, correlation and path coefficient analyses, as well as principal component analysis (PCA). The results revealed significant genotypic variation and differential trait expression between the two production systems, with the relative contribution of agro-morphological traits to grain yield varying between production systems. Integrated analysis of genetic variability, correlation, path coefficient analysis, and principal component analysis identified production system-specific trait combinations associated with grain yield. Under the conventional production system, flag leaf breadth (FLB), number of productive tillers per plant (NPTP), hundred seed weight (HSW), and flag leaf length (FLL) were prominent traits, with strong positive direct effects in path analysis, whereas leaf area (LA), NPTP, HSW, plant height (PH), and days to 50% flowering (DFF) were prominent under the organic production system, also showing positive direct effects in path analysis. Genotypic best linear unbiased prediction (BLUP) estimates identified Ponmani samba (G40), Varakkal (G60), and Sengalapattu sirumani (G49) with the highest yield BLUP estimates under the organic production system, whereas Mani samba (G29), TKM1 (G80), and Bavani (G6) showed the highest yield BLUP estimates under the conventional production system. Milagu samba (G31), Polinel (G39), and Ponmani samba (G40) consistently ranked among the top-performing genotypes based on yield BLUP estimates across both production systems, indicating their potential as breeding materials for further evaluation.
n642bd57f6303: A substantial fraction of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS)-associated proteins remains poorly characterized, in part because of the limited availability of validated research antibodies. We established knockout (KO)-based antibody characterization workflows and demonstrated that widely used antibodies against the major ALS-associated protein C9orf72 lacked specificity (Laflamme et al., 2019). We subsequently scaled this framework to systematically benchmark research antibodies, revealing that up to 61% fail to perform as recommended by manufacturers (Ayoubi et al., 2023b). Here, we extend this approach by establishing the ALS-Reproducible Antibody Platform (ALS-RAP), a comprehensive effort to generate a publicly available dataset of KO-validated antibodies targeting proteins encoded by ALS risk genes. In total, we characterized 303 antibodies against 33 ALS-associated proteins to identify high-quality reagents for use in western blot, immunoprecipitation, and immunofluorescence. Using these antibodies, we profiled protein levels across human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived and primary neurological cell types. These analyses revealed diverse cellular distributions and higher levels of several ALS-associated proteins in glial populations, consistent with emerging evidence for immune contributions to ALS. Together, ALS-RAP provides a validated antibody toolbox and protein expression resource to support the study of ALS-associated proteins.
n09891904aa78: Insect olfaction is facilitated by a heterotetrameric odorant receptor–odorant receptor co-receptor (OR-Orco) complex. However, extensive sequence divergence and lineage-specific expansion have complicated large-scale comparisons of OR repertoires across insects. Here, we integrated sequence similarity, structural similarity, and molecular docking to analyze ORs from 115 insect species. OR repertoire size was associated with adult diet, larval diet, and habitat, but not with circadian rhythm. We developed a ‘trunk–branch’ network framework to classify ORs according to sequence and structural similarity and used large-scale molecular docking to derive comparative docking profiles. Despite marked differences in sequence- and structural-community composition, almost all sampled orders contained ORs assigned to all six docking-profile communities. Holometabolous insects showed higher OR sequence-community diversity than non-holometabolous insects, and docking-profile composition differed between extant lineages whose order-level origins predate or postdate the end-Permian mass extinction. Most notably, we identified a highly conserved extracellular β-sheet in Orco that restricts ligand access to the binding pocket and may contribute to its reduced capacity to bind natural odorants. The emergence of Orco represents a key evolutionary transition from homomeric receptors to heteromeric OR–Orco complexes, and our results suggest that this transition may have been accompanied by pronounced specialization of the extracellular domain and binding pocket. Together, these analyses provide a class-wide framework for comparing insect OR diversity and generate testable hypotheses for future experimental and evolutionary studies.
n6c6f6731ed94: Tumorigenesis typically follows a multi-hit trajectory, driven by accumulating oncogenic mutations. Colorectal cancer (CRC) has long served as a paradigmatic model of multi-hit tumorigenesis, characterized by adenoma-carcinoma transition accompanied by acquisition of specific oncogene and tumor suppressor mutations. However, how the temporal order of early mutations influences CRC initiation remains poorly understood. To address this, we established a CRC tumorigenesis model using murine intestinal organoids. By introducing defined combinations of key CRC driver mutations (Kras, Apc, and Trp53) in distinct orders, we systematically investigated how the order of mutation accumulation affects tumor initiation. Our results reveal that the mutation accumulation confers growth advantages in both in vitro and in vivo models. Strikingly, mutation order also influenced the tumorigenic properties of the organoids. Whereas organoids with Trp53 loss before or after Apc loss similarly affected organoid phenotypes in vitro or tumorigenicity in immunodeficient mice, organoids with Trp53 loss preceding Apc inactivation exhibited reduced tumor-forming potential in immunocompetent mice, likely due to their distinct immunological features. Collectively, our study reveals a critical role of ordered mutation accumulation in CRC initiation, an insight that may hold clinical relevance.
n9cb58d149cc9: Scientific progress depends on reliable and reproducible results. Progress can be accelerated when data are shared and re-analyzed to address new questions. Current approaches to storing and analyzing neural data involve bespoke formats and software that make replication and reuse of data difficult. To address these challenges, we created Spyglass, an open-source data management and analysis framework written in Python. Spyglass provides reproducible pipelines for common neuroscience analyses and sharing of raw data, intermediate analyses, and final results within and across labs. Spyglass uses the Neurodata Without Borders (NWB) standard and includes pipelines for spectral filtering, spike sorting, pose tracking, and neural decoding. Spyglass can be extended to apply existing and newly developed pipelines to datasets from multiple sources. We demonstrate these features in the context of a cross-laboratory replication by applying advanced state space decoding algorithms to publicly available data. New users can try out Spyglass on a Jupyter Hub hosted by HHMI and 2i2c: https://spyglass.hhmi.2i2c.cloud/.
n0a6eefc1cd1d: This article reviews the risk-based literature on international arbitrage deviations, exchange rates, and countries’ borrowing costs. It synthesizes recent work identifying policy uncertainty as a key primitive in risk-based models of global finance and investment. Volatile and unpredictable policy environments alter forward-looking investors’ expectations and portfolio decisions, thereby influencing exchange rates, excess currency returns, and the cost of capital—effects especially pronounced in emerging markets. We discuss how increased global policy uncertainty can create conditions under which a policy risk premium also arises for the US dollar. We present preliminary evidence consistent with this hypothesis.
nd3fa721bf990: In the face of global challenges, corporate boards may need to think differently. In this review, I explore how the finance literature addresses the challenges boards face. I focus on a key recent challenge: how boards navigate shifting expectations about their objectives beyond shareholder value. I highlight that the literatures on boards’ stakeholder objectives and diversity overlap. This raises interesting, and important, questions about how boards can develop “new thinking” more generally. Much research remains to be done in this area. To rise to the challenge, however, finance academia may also need to think differently. Using data that measure how individual directors think, I illustrate that many factors may influence how directors think, including selection. Recognizing path dependencies in approaches and assumptions may help the field of finance continue to generate influential research on boards.
n7c12e793126e: This article provides an overview of the literature on financial literacy. It covers the initial measurement that created the Big Three financial literacy questions and measures of personal finance knowledge featuring 28 questions. It shows that levels of financial literacy are low and have not been improving over time. This is true not only in the United States but also in countries worldwide. These findings matter because financial literacy is conducive to savvy financial behaviors, from holding precautionary savings to planning for retirement to many other financial decisions. Financial education programs have grown exponentially over time, providing important insights into their cost-effectiveness. Personal finance courses have been added to high school and college curricula, and the evidence indicates that they are useful initiatives to improve financial knowledge and downstream behavior.
na5f0345cd475: This article reviews the literature that uses survey data to study expectation formation among investors. We begin by outlining methods for eliciting investor beliefs and summarizing key empirical patterns documented in recent work. Highlighting the persistent cross-sectional heterogeneity in expectations, we then review evidence on the determinants of beliefs, including a new analysis of belief reactions to the tariff announcement in April 2025. Next, we examine how expectations shape financial decision-making, emphasizing the systematic but muted sensitivity of outcomes to belief changes. We conclude by pointing to promising directions for future research on belief measurement, the determinants of expectations, and their implications for policy makers.
n261944e0c527: This article surveys recent developments and important issues in option pricing with a particular focus on time-varying volatility and tail risks. We start by briefly reviewing the most important market events, financial innovations, and theoretical developments from the 1970s to the 1990s and then focus on a more detailed review of the current state of knowledge with a discussion of open questions.
n0be1ea3ca0d8: Recent research suggests that corporate debt contracts in the modern economy follow two common approaches: Some contracts lend against the liquidation value of separable assets, while others focus on cash flows from operations and the going-concern value of the firm as a whole. This article summarizes the key contract features and default resolution mechanisms of these two types of debt used by nonfinancial firms. Firms with abundant liquidation values and physical assets rely on the former; firms with low liquidation values and limited physical assets resort to the latter. Among large firms and those with positive earnings, total borrowing does not depend on physical assets, whereas among small firms and those with negative earnings, total borrowing remains dependent on physical assets. The evidence sheds light on the evolving nature of debt contracting and financial intermediation, with implications for economic fluctuations and growth.
n01710943e162: The myogenic tone and thus diameter of brain arterioles varies on multiple time scales. These variations result from coordinated contraction and relaxation of electrically coupled smooth muscle cells in the arteriole wall that drive constriction. A prominent feature is a broad-band ∼0.1 Hz rhythmicity, designated vasomotion, in the pial arterioles spanning the cortical mantle and the penetrating arterioles that nourish the capillary bed. As characterized in the murine brain, vasomotion supports propagating waves with a typical wavelength of 20 mm (a speed of 2 mm/s) that modulate perfusion with a magnitude equal to that of functional hyperemia. The spectral and spatial properties reflect the interaction of smooth muscle dynamics with the underlying neuronal drive. Possible functional roles of vasomotion are to mitigate capillary stalls and to facilitate the exchange of solutes between interstitial and cerebrospinal fluid. Indeed, loss of vasomotion has been implicated in the pathophysiology of vascular disease, such as cerebral amyloid angiopathy.
n95b7c534650f: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is characterized by epithelial barrier disruption, mucosal immune activation, and sustained intestinal inflammation. We developed a biologically interpretable public-transcriptomic signature using Gene Expression Omnibus datasets GSE75214, GSE38713, and GSE92415. A literature-curated panel of 35 mucosal barrier injury-related genes was integrated with differential expression, LASSO regression, random forest prioritization, and ridge logistic regression. Six genes (LCN2, DEFB1, S100A8, MUC1, VIL1, and TJP3) were retained as a locked transcriptomic score. Because the original feature-selection steps used the complete development cohort, we added 50 repetitions of stratified five-fold outer cross-validation. All preprocessing and ridge tuning were restricted to each outer-training fold; the locked score achieved a mean out-of-fold AUC of 0.9660 (SD 0.0031). A stricter sensitivity analysis that repeated differential-expression filtering, LASSO, random-forest ranking, deterministic six-gene selection, and ridge fitting within each outer-training fold achieved a mean out-of-fold AUC of 0.9600 (SD 0.0094). The refitted locked model retained discrimination in GSE38713 (AUC 0.8974, 95% CI 0.8040–0.9909) and GSE92415 (AUC 0.9894, 95% CI 0.9744–1.0000) when one development-derived cutoff was applied unchanged. The six-gene score did not significantly outperform VIL1 alone in the development cohort (DeLong P = 0.4026). The signature should therefore be interpreted as a molecular pattern associated with UC mucosal inflammation and barrier remodeling rather than as a UC-specific clinical diagnostic test.
na07ab7bfae83: The county high school policies (CHSPs) is crucial for improving the quality of basic education in China’s counties and promoting rural social development. As policy documents are the foundational elements of policy systems, it is crucial to evaluate current policy texts, identify their shortcomings, and provide empirical evidence for future policy development. This study collected 55 policy texts from provincial and municipal governments, utilizing the Policy Modeling Consistency index model to evaluate 14 representative policies. The results indicate that all the assessed policies fall within the“pass”,“good”,or“with distinction” score category, with no substandard policies identified and none achieving a “perfect” score.A detailed analysis identifies critical policy shortcomings, including the prioritization of short-to-medium-term strategies over long-term planning, fragmented enrollment systems, insufficient campus culture development, as well as limited career guidance, mental health support,and policy guidance for home-school-community joint education. Local governments adopt a conservative stance on educational policy evaluation and systemic institutional reforms.To address these issues, this study recommends that local governments integrate the enrollment systems of public and private high schools within their jurisdictions, strengthen the prohibition of on cross-regional enrollment, increase investment in students’ career guidance and mental health education, and launch more programs to encourage parents and communities to participate in school education. Moreover, the central government should urge local authorities to accelerate reforms in the high school education system.
n541f7ddfa3cf: The rapid growth of the Internet has made network attacks increasingly frequent, stealthy, and diverse, posing stringent requirements on the accuracy and latency of network intrusion detection systems (NIDS). Although deep-learning-based NIDS can achieve strong detection performance, their large parameter size and high computational cost hinder deployment on resource-constrained edge devices. To address this limitation, we propose a temperature-adaptive logit-standardized knowledge distillation framework for lightweight network intrusion detection. A high-capacity teacher network first learns discriminative representations from network traffic, and a compact student network is then trained to mimic the teacher under a tailored distillation scheme. During distillation, we apply per-sample Z-score standardization to the logits of both teacher and student models to mitigate scale mismatch and emphasize relative inter-class relationships. Moreover, we adapt the distillation temperature according to sample difficulty and training progress, enabling suitably smoothed soft targets across samples and stages, and jointly optimize the student with hard-label supervision. Experiments on benchmark datasets including NSL-KDD and CIC-IDS2017 demonstrate that the proposed method substantially reduces model complexity while maintaining stable and competitive detection performance. Additional repeated-run, ablation, and lightweight baseline analyses further indicate that the proposed framework achieves a favorable accuracy–complexity trade-off.
n9015e9feeffb: Artificial intelligence (AI)–driven chatbots based on large language models are increasingly entering medical education, but evidence on the real-world use of domestic systems such as DeepSeek among Chinese medical interns is still scarce. This cross-sectional study investigated the prevalence, patterns and perceptions of DeepSeek use among medical interns at the Second Affiliated Hospital of Anhui Medical University. A total of 634 interns from clinical medicine, preventive medicine and nursing completed an anonymous questionnaire. Overall, about one-third of interns reported using DeepSeek. Among users, most engaged with the tool regularly, with over half using it several times per week. DeepSeek was primarily employed for completing assignments, searching for information, translation and polishing of written texts, while a smaller subset of users reported using it for data analysis. Attitudes toward DeepSeek were mainly neutral or optimistic, and across majors most users perceived its advantages and disadvantages as broadly balanced, while only a minority considered the disadvantages to outweigh the advantages. After adjustment, residence and major remained associated with DeepSeek use, whereas age and sex were not. Urban interns were more likely to report using DeepSeek than rural interns. Compared with clinical medicine interns, preventive medicine interns were less likely to report use, whereas nursing interns were more likely to do so. Among users, overall attitudes differed across majors, while usage frequency and the perceived balance of advantages and disadvantages did not. These findings provide descriptive evidence on the use and evaluation of DeepSeek among medical interns and may inform future institutional guidance on responsible use, verification of AI-generated information and academic integrity.
n925eea0fdf2f: Reliable joint perception of crop rows, furrows, and obstacles is essential for autonomous inter-row operations in seedling-stage cotton fields. However, small and sparsely distributed plants, perspective-convergent rows, irregular furrow boundaries, and low obstacle pixel coverage jointly challenge fine-detail preservation, long-range structural modeling, and boundary discrimination under real-time constraints. This study formulated cotton-field perception as a four-class semantic segmentation task and constructed a dataset of 709 pixel-wise annotated images comprising background, crop rows, furrows, and obstacles. We developed Agri-PIDNet-S, a field-specific lightweight network based on PIDNet-S. A coordinate-aware multi-kernel inverted residual module (CA-MKIR) preserves shallow details and small-obstacle contours, a squeeze-and-excitation-enhanced deep-to-token module (SaE-D2T) models long-range row and furrow structures, and a boundary-guided window-attention refinement Bag (BWR-Bag) improves semantic–boundary fusion. The network was trained with a composite loss incorporating auxiliary boundary supervision. On the cotton-field test set, Agri-PIDNet-S achieved 92.37% mean intersection over union (mIoU) and 96.02% mean Dice coefficient (mDice) in the model-comparison experiment, while repeated training with three seeds yielded an mIoU of 92.35 ± 0.03%. Relative to PIDNet-S under the same comparison protocol, mIoU increased by 3.53 percentage points, while obstacle IoU improved from 79.60% to 88.67%. The model contained 8.048 million parameters, required 19.161 GFLOPs, and achieved 155.67 frames per second. Zero-shot external evaluation on tomato, watermelon, and maize fields yielded a structural mIoU of 86.29% for the background, crop-row, and furrow classes. Under the evaluated conditions, the task-oriented modifications achieved higher segmentation point estimates than PIDNet-S while maintaining computational efficiency; the external results provide preliminary evidence of cross-crop structural transfer.
n4d8b1bb06d20: Background Urogenital schistosomiasis (UGS) remains a significant public health issue in Tanzania, co-infection with urinary tract infections (UTIs) can complicate diagnosis due to overlapping symptoms. Additionally, gastrointestinal carriage of multidrug-resistant bacteria (MDRB) increases risks of self-infection and transmission to others. Primary school-aged children in rural settings are particularly at risk for both diseases due to poor water sanitation and risky behaviors. This study reports the prevalence and patterns of UGS and UTI co-infection, and MDRB gut carriage among primary school-aged children. Methodology A school-based cross-sectional study was conducted in Meatu district, Tanzania (Oct–Dec 2024). UGS was diagnosed using urine filtration, UTIs through urine culture while stool samples were screened for Extended spectrum beta lactamase (ESBL) producing bacteria. Descriptive analysis was done using STATA 15.0. Results Among 405 children enrolled, the prevalence of UGS, UTIs, and UGS–UTI co-infection was 44.1%, 12.8%, and 5.2%, respectively. Heavy UGS infection was associated with a greater likelihood of UTI than light infection. Haematuria was associated with UGS, whereas frequent and painful urination were common among children with UTIs and co-infection. Escherichia coli was the predominant UTI pathogen, with substantial resistance to third-generation cephalosporins. ESBL-producing bacteria and multidrug-resistant bacteria were also identified among UTI isolates. Conclusions Co-infection of UGS & UTI among primary school children is a noticeable problem in the study settings; fever, frequent urination and painful urination are good predictors for co-infection. Similarities in clinical symptoms among co-infected individuals may complicate diagnosis and management on the initial assessment. High proportion of MDRB carriage in rural settings indicates the extensive burden of antimicrobial resistance in developing countries.
n7496961b7ae3: Objective To assess cardiometabolic risk burden among schoolchildren aged 7–10 years attending public urban elementary schools in the Federal District, Brazil, and examine its association with health behaviours and socioeconomic characteristics. Methods This population-based cross-sectional study included 978 children, with a subsample of 315 undergoing biochemical assessment. Data were collected on dietary intake, eating and sedentary behaviours, physical activity, anthropometry, blood pressure, and biochemical markers. A composite cardiometabolic risk outcome was constructed and assessed only in the biochemical subsample. Analyses accounted for the complex sampling design. Results Among children included in the biochemical subsample, 89.9% presented at least one cardiometabolic risk factor and dyslipidaemia was present in 72.0%. In the full sample, overweight was observed in 30.2% of the children. Eating with distractions was associated with higher odds of cardiometabolic risk burden, increasing the likelihood of one to two risk factors (odds ratio = 2.98; 95% confidence interval: 1.62–5.47) and three or more risk factors (odds ratio = 2.52; 95% confidence interval:1.08–5.90). Consuming snacks or treats, compared with a homemade meal, was associated with lower odds of presenting one to two risk factors (odds ratio = 0.32; 95% confidence interval: 0.10–0.99), but no association was observed with three or more risk factors. Conclusions Within the non-random biochemical subsample of morning-shift students, a high burden of cardiometabolic risk factors was observed, and eating with distractions was associated with greater cardiometabolic risk burden. Early preventive strategies targeting modifiable behaviours are needed.
nb51a6d0d09a5: This study evaluated the effect of adding chickpea flour to milk-based formulations on physicochemical parameters, the survival, and viability of potentially probiotic microorganisms. Four formulations were prepared using skimmed milk (10%) and sucrose (10%), each containing Lactobacillus plantarum S180.7 (CF1) or L. plantarum SBR64.7 (CF2), with or without 4.5% chickpea flour (TF1 and TF2). Composition, physicochemical properties, total phenolic content, antioxidant activity, and bacterial viability were assessed during 24 hours of fermentation and 28 days of storage at 4°C. Formulations with chickpea flour exhibited a greater pH decrease (ΔpH, 24–0 h: TF1 = –1.81 and TF2 = –1.38) than controls (CF1 = –0.58 and CF2 = –0.52), along with higher titratable acidity after 6 and 9 hours, respectively. Chickpea flour enhanced bacterial growth, reaching 8 Log CFU/mL, and increased phenolic content without affecting antioxidant potential. Viability remained stable and higher than controls, confirming improved probiotic stability in milk-based formulations.
n41b1db8743e6: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) represents a major cause of non-traumatic lower-limb amputation and is associated with substantial morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs. Despite advances in medical and revascularization therapies, major amputations remain frequent, and comprehensive nationwide estimates of their clinical and hospital-related economic burden within the Italian National Health Service (SSN) are limited. The objectives of this study were to estimate the hospital-related economic burden of major lower-limb amputations attributable to PAD in Italy and to assess revascularization patterns and in-hospital mortality within the SSN. We conducted a nationwide observational study using the Italian National Hospital Discharge Database. Acute hospital discharges between 2015 and 2021 with a major lower-limb amputation and Diagnosis Related Group 113 were identified. Inpatient volumes, length of stay, and costs were estimated by amputation level. A longitudinal cohort of patients amputated between 2015 and 2017 was followed for two years before and after the index hospitalization to assess prior revascularization and in-hospital mortality using age- and sex-adjusted Cox models. A total of 26,417 PAD-attributable major amputations were identified, 75.6% of which were above-knee procedures. Cumulative inpatient expenditure reached €294 million, corresponding to over 511,000 hospital days. Only 46.0% of patients underwent revascularization before amputation. In-hospital mortality increased steeply within the first six months post-amputation and remained higher after above-knee procedures and among patients with diabetes, reaching 16–25% at 180 days and 23–34% at two years. Major lower-limb amputation remains a severe and costly outcome of PAD in Italy. Improved implementation of guideline-recommended PAD management is needed to reduce avoidable amputations and their economic burden on the SSN.
n53ccc187f72c: We investigated aqueous humor (AH) cytokine profiles in first- and second-operated eyes of patients undergoing sequential bilateral cataract surgery and explored these profiles according to diabetes mellitus (DM) status. This retrospective, within-subject, comparative observational study included 71 patients, comprising 39 without DM and 32 with DM but without diabetic retinopathy, who underwent uneventful sequential bilateral cataract surgery within a 2-week interval. The concentrations of vascular endothelial growth factor, angiopoietin-2, placental growth factor, interleukin (IL)-6, IL-8, monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (MCP-1), and transforming growth factor–β2 (TGF-β2) in the AH were analyzed. In patients without DM, mean IL-6 concentrations were nominally lower in the second eye than in the first eye (P = 0.041), although this finding did not remain statistically significant after FDR adjustment. In patients with DM, there were no significant differences in cytokine concentrations between the first and second eyes. The eye-order × DM interaction for IL-6 was not statistically significant (P = 0.644). Compared with patients without DM, higher MCP-1 and TGF-β2 concentrations were observed in the first eye and higher TGF-β2 concentrations in the second eye, with the strongest statistical evidence observed for first-eye TGF-β2, which remained significant after FDR adjustment. Differences in AH cytokine profiles were observed between patients with and without DM during sequential bilateral cataract surgery. The lower mean IL-6 concentration observed in the second eyes of patients without diabetes represents a novel, although exploratory, observation. Whether this finding reflects pre-existing inter-eye variability or a biological response associated with sequential surgery remains to be determined.
na75b3988b02a: Introduction Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is an effective and lifesaving intervention against cervical cancer. However, achieving high, equitable, and sustainable uptake remains a significant challenge in low-resource settings, including Ethiopia. Therefore, this study aimed to explore the enablers and barriers to HPV vaccination implementation in Ethiopia. Methods An interpretive descriptive qualitative design was employed in purposively selected settings representing diverse socio-ecological contexts (Afar, Amhara, Addis Ababa, and Dire Dawa). Six focus group discussions were conducted with adolescent girls (n = 14), parents of eligible adolescent girls (n = 14), and community representatives (n = 14). In addition, nineteen key informant interviews (KIIs) were conducted with healthcare providers, Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI) coordinators, and technical advisors from governmental and non-governmental organizations. Data were analysed using a combined deductive–inductive content analysis guided by the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR 2.0). Results Multiple interacting factors influenced HPV vaccination implementation in Ethiopia, categorised as enablers and barriers across community, health system, and policy levels. Enablers included the Perceived Vaccine Attributes and Delivery Adaptability, Supportive Policy and Multisectoral Strategic Partnerships, Socio-cultural and Belief-based Drivers, and Health System Readiness and Workforce Motivation. However, several barriers limited implementation, including Suspicions About Targeting 9–14-year-old Girls and Consent-related Administrative Obstacles, Pervasive Misinformation and Cognitive Resistance, Health System Resource Constraints and Coordination Gaps, Donor Dependency Risks and Financial Sustainability Concerns, and Structural Access Constraints and Equity Gaps. Conclusions While policy shifts, external strategic partnerships, and frontline worker dedication have accelerated vaccine reach, the long-term sustainability of Ethiopia’s HPV vaccination program remains constrained by multi-level barriers. Progress toward the global 2030 cervical cancer elimination targets requires trust-building risk-communication strategies to counter fertility myths, simplified consent procedures, targeted domestic resource mobilization, and context-specific delivery models tailored to underserved pastoralist and urban sub-populations.
n4557b88d3175: by Kelsey C. Smith, David Navarro, Julie A. Blanchong Wild turkeys (Meleagris gallopavo) were nearly extirpated in the early 1900’s and extensive restoration efforts utilizing translocated wild turkeys were employed to restore populations. Although these efforts were successful, populations have again been in decline due to unknown causes. Lymphoproliferative disease virus (LPDV) was first detected in the United States in 2009. The coinciding appearance of LDPV and declining populations have led to studies in several states and provinces in North America to characterize its prevalence and distribution due to concerns about its potential role in population declines. The spread of disease agents is a common outcome during translocation programs and could be related to the spread of LPDV. Prior studies have performed phylogenetic analyses to examine genetic variation across and geographic clustering among strains. In this study we aimed to identify the diversity of LPDV strains present in wild turkeys in Iowa and if there was geographic clustering within the state or with other locations where LPDV has been detected. We sequenced a subset (n = 77) of hunter-harvested samples covering eight of the nine agricultural regions in Iowa that tested PCR positive with the viral gag gene. We performed phylogenetic analysis on 73 unique Iowan strains as well as previously catalogued strains from other regions retrieved from the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) GenBank database. Overall, Iowa strains did not show geographic clustering within the state or with any other specific geographic regions. Our study demonstrated that there is a high level of genetic diversity among LPDV strains in Iowa and did not provide evidence of connection with a particular location external to Iowa as a source of introduction of LPDV to the state.
nf71ee8be2d50: by Fatima M. Damagum, Amina H. Hassan, Andrew E. Uloko, Hauwa A. Habeeb, Hadiza B. Damagum, Zainab A. Umar, Hassan A. Murtala, Zainab Abdulkadir, Ibrahim Y. Ibrahim, Zainab U. Ibrahim, Umar F. Abdullahi, Hamisu M. Salihu, Muktar H. Aliyu, Phylis J. Kanki, Baba M. Musa Background Female sexual dysfunction (FSD) is a recognised complication of diabetes mellitus (DM), but evidence on its clinical and biological correlates in sub-Saharan Africa remains limited. FSD is defined as a disorder characterized by disturbances in sexual desire, arousal, orgasm, and/or pain that causes interpersonal difficulty or distress. This study examined associations between glycaemic control, reproductive hormonal status, and FSD among premenopausal women with diabetes in northern Nigeria. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional study among 180 premenopausal women aged 18–45 years attending diabetes clinics at two tertiary hospitals in Kano, Nigeria. Sexual function was assessed using the Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI), with scores ≤26 indicating FSD. Glycaemic control was measured using glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c), categorised as optimal (≤7.0%) or suboptimal (>7.0%). Reproductive hormones (FSH, LH, Oestrogen, testosterone, prolactin, and progesterone) were measured at phase-specific points of the menstrual cycle. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to assess associations with FSD, and linear regression models were used to examine associations with FSFI domain scores. Results Overall, 51.7% of participants screened positive for FSD. Suboptimal glycaemic control was associated with higher odds of FSD (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] 2.80; 95% CI 1.05–7.72). It was also associated with lower orgasm (β −0.77; p = 0.032) and satisfaction (β −0.88; p = 0.003) scores. No statistically significant associations were observed between reproductive hormonal imbalance (including FSH, LH, Oestrogen, testosterone, prolactin, and progesterone) and FSD or FSFI domain scores. Conclusions FSD was common among premenopausal women with diabetes in this setting. Suboptimal glycaemic control was associated with FSD and with lower orgasm and satisfaction scores, while reproductive hormonal measures were not associated with FSD. These findings provide evidence on clinical correlates of FSD in a sub-Saharan African population.
n3fff9e9bf2d3: This exploratory pilot study asked whether frontal alpha asymmetry (FAA) recorded while a price is displayed varies with the satisfaction-rating change a consumer then makes. Twenty-one participants completed two blocks of 30 trials: view a product, give a pre-price rating (1–9), see the price, give a post-price rating, which they were instructed to change except at the scale limits. The change is described by its direction and magnitude (|Δ|, provisionally labeled Decision Momentum), two descriptions of one difference score. FAA was computed from relative alpha power at F3/F4 over 0–3 s after price onset on average-referenced data. Inference rests on 19 participants and 820 trials. The primary pooled test of the direction × magnitude interaction was inconclusive (β=−0.051, 95% CI [−0.111,0.009], p = 0.093). An exploratory block-stratified analysis found an interaction in the first block (β=−0.087, 95% CI [−0.152,−0.021], p = 0.010), although neither of its two component slopes differed clearly from zero. Support varied across specifications, and five alternative operationalizations of FAA did not reproduce it. The same model applied to the window before price onset, where the predictors cannot yet reflect the price, produced an interaction of comparable or larger size pooled and in the second block. In the first block, the direct comparison did not establish a difference between windows, and adjusting for pre-price FAA left the first-block estimate unchanged (p = 0.008); in the second block, the two windows did differ (p = 0.021), the association being present before the price and not after it. Single-trial classification of change direction showed modest performance with uncertain generalizability (ROC AUC 0.538; participant bootstrap 95% CI [0.476, 0.564]). The association is reported as hypothesis-generating; attributing it specifically to price-related processing is not supported by these data.
n82a08506d402: Background 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural (5-HMF), a ubiquitous furan derivative formed during the thermal processing of carbohydrate-rich foods, represents a widespread dietary exposure. However, its potential contribution to idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) remains unclear. This study investigated the molecular links between 5-HMF and IPF using an integrated computational and experimental approach. Methods IPF-related genes were identified through transcriptomic analysis combining differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis. Candidate targets were obtained by intersecting IPF-associated genes with predicted 5-HMF targets. Functional enrichment analysis, ensemble machine learning, and SHAP interpretation were performed to prioritize candidate targets, while molecular docking was used to explore potential 5-HMF–target interactions. A bleomycin-induced mouse model of pulmonary fibrosis was further used to evaluate the effects of 5-HMF on fibrotic lung injury and the transcriptional expression of prioritized candidate genes. Results A total of 1,776 IPF-associated genes and 143 predicted 5-HMF targets were identified, yielding 12 overlapping candidate targets. Enrichment analysis implicated these genes in fibrosis-related pathways, including chemical carcinogenesis–receptor activation and estrogen signaling. Machine learning analysis prioritized seven core targets (CA2, CA4, ESR2, F10, HSP90AA1, PLA2G1B, and PTPRB), all of which accommodated 5-HMF in their orthosteric pockets in blind docking, albeit with weak, non-selective Vina scores (−4.5 to −5.4 kcal/mol). In vivo, 5-HMF significantly exacerbated bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis, as demonstrated by aggravated lung injury, increased collagen deposition, and elevated expression of Hsp90aa1, Pla2g1b, Ca4, F10, Acta2, and Col1a1. Conclusion Our findings suggest that 5-HMF may exacerbate fibrotic lung injury through multiple fibrosis-related molecular targets and pathways. These findings provide preliminary evidence for a potential association between 5-HMF exposure and the aggravation of pulmonary fibrosis, while further studies are required to determine whether 5-HMF can independently initiate fibrotic pathology.
n4c5d121c4067: Background Drug overdose is a leading cause of death among people released from correctional facilities, and the risk of overdose is higher among people living with HIV (PLWH). Overdose remains understudied in people in South Africa despite the high burden of HIV and hazardous opioid use. The researchers aimed to qualitatively explore how formerly incarcerated people living with HIV and OUD in South Africa understand, experience, and respond to overdose. Methods People with HIV and self-reported hazardous opioid use prior to correctional facility release or shortly after release were enrolled in a convenience sample. Twenty-three formerly incarcerated people living with HIV and opioid use in or around Tshwane, South Africa completed sequential in-depth interviews that explored medication-assisted treatment for hazardous opioid use and HIV care delivery. Transcripts were analyzed thematically using both deductive and inductive coding, with a focus on participants’ knowledge and definition of overdose, personal experiences with overdose, and responses to overdose. Results All participants used the term “overdose”, but there was no unified understanding of what constitutes an overdose or how to manage an overdose. The period immediately following release from incarceration was identified as a key moment in which overdose occurred. Pouring water onto the person overdosing was reported to be the most prevalent response strategy. Only two participants contacted or watched their peers contact the ambulance. Fear of law enforcement involvement was perceived as a barrier to calling for emergency services. Conclusion The findings identify a gap in overdose knowledge among corrections-involved people living with HIV and hazardous opioid use in South Africa. There is a need to increase knowledge regarding overdose recognition and responses.
n7f2901ef3c85: Background Sepsis remains a leading cause of death in intensive care units worldwide and may be accompanied by complex complications, including encephalopathy, coagulopathy, acute kidney injury, myocardial dysfunction, and delirium, each of which substantially increases the risk of poor outcomes. Machine learning, a promising approach for prognostic prediction, can capture complex nonlinear relationships among clinical risk factors. However, its predictive performance in sepsis and its specific complications remains unclear. Method We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library for relevant literature through April 2026. Studies that aimed to develop or validate machine learning models to predict mortality in adult patients with sepsis and its associated complications were included. The random-effects or bivariate model was used to calculate the AUC, sensitivity, and specificity. Results Overall, machine learning models show moderate predictive performance for short-term mortality in sepsis, with a combined AUC of 0.82 for the training set (46 studies, 15 models) and 0.79 for the validation set (50 studies, 25 models). Logistic regression is the most widely evaluated model, demonstrating stable performance (validation AUC = 0.81). Integrated methods, including random forest and XGBoost, performed equally well, with AUCs between 0.81 and 0.83 in both groups. Although LightGBM and DL-CMT achieved the highest AUCs in the training and validation sets, respectively, both estimates were based on a single study.Among the complications, the evidence for sepsis-associated encephalopathy (AUC = 0.81, 3 studies) and sepsis-induced coagulopathy (AUC = 0.80, 4 studies) is the most conclusive and best demonstrated. Sepsis-associated acute kidney injury showed moderate and stable performance (validation AUC = 0.79, 4 studies). Sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy showed significant attenuation from training to validation (AUC 0.84 vs 0.78, all from a single study), and random forest performed well in training (AUC = 0.98) but was not widely reported. Septic shock reached the highest AUC (0.95), but this was based on a single study. The predictive utility of sepsis-associated delirium is limited (AUC = 0.67, 1 study), and sepsis-induced myocardial injury is moderate (AUC = 0.77, 1 study).For long-term mortality, evidence is extremely lacking. Only SAE (AUC 0.88 during training and 0.86 during validation) and SCRS (combined AUC 0.76) provided single study estimates, ruling out reliable conclusions. Conclusion In this meta-analysis, machine learning models showed moderate predictive performance for short-term mortality in sepsis. Among complications, SAE and SIC had the strongest evidence and best performance, whereas SAD showed limited utility. Evidence for long-term mortality was extremely scarce. These findings support the potential role of machine learning in early prognostic risk stratification, yet they also highlight the urgent need for rigorous external validation and higher-quality studies, particularly for under-investigated complications.
n9cff814c44d1: Student retention intention remains a concern for higher education systems worldwide and is relevant to institutional sustainability and Sustainable Development Goal 4 (SDG 4). The proposed relationships were examined using structural equation modeling with SmartPLS 4. The results indicate that perceived quality teaching is positively associated with student retention intention, both directly and indirectly through students’ knowledge, skills, and competencies and student loyalty. Significant indirect associations were identified through each mediator separately and through the proposed serial mediation pathway. These findings highlight the relevance of considering students’ perceived capability development and institutional attachment together when examining retention intention. HCT provides a rationale for the relationship between perceived teaching quality and students’ knowledge, skills, competencies, while EVT offers an interpretive perspective; however, expectancy of success and subjective task value were not directly measured. The cross-sectional design also precludes conclusions about temporal ordering or causality. Practically, the findings suggest that faculty development, student-centered pedagogies, digitally supported teaching, and curriculum alignment with labor market needs merit consideration in institutional quality assurance. The findings provide context-specific evidence from Pakistani higher education (HE) and are relevant to SDG 4 through their focus on perceived teaching quality and students’ intentions to continue their studies. They do not establish effects on actual retention or broader educational outcomes.
ne76ce7f55560: Emotions are based on evolutionarily conserved building blocks (‘emotion primitives’) that are present across mammals. Wildtype and transgenic flies were subjected to various conditions prior to behavioural testing. The results indicate that wall-following and total walking activity are independent measures that are modulated, with generally increased wall-following observed under aversive stimuli and decreased values under positive conditions, independent of the time of day. Activation of reward-related neurons decreased wall-following while inhibition increased it. Moreover, treatment with ethanol or diazepam produced predictable changes in behaviour. Our findings suggest that Drosophila shares conserved core emotion-like building blocks with vertebrates, and show that wall-following and total walking activity in the OFT can serve as a reliable indicator of emotional valence and arousal in the fruit fly. This positions Drosophila as a powerful genetic model to dissect the neuronal and neurochemical substrates of emotion primitives.
nc6d1ca87b2cb: TAT (twin-arginine translocation) is a preprotein translocation system dedicated to membrane translocation of prefolded proteins in plants and bacteria. Our findings in recombinant Escherichia coli demonstrate that overproducing TatABC increases MPIase levels, and that depleting MPIase results in TAT precursor accumulation in the cytosol. Furthermore, co-reconstitution of MPIase with TatABC revealed the translocation activities of TAT substrates in a proton motive force-dependent manner. This is the first successful reconstitution of the TAT system and will be advantageous for understanding its mechanisms.
n3f0de375e032: Macrophages are driven to form distinct functional phenotypes in response to different immunological stimuli, in a process widely referred to as macrophage polarization. Toward this, we configure an integrative network analysis pipeline that utilizes macrophage transcriptomes in response to 28 distinct stimuli, reconstructs contextualized human gene regulatory networks, and identifies epicenters of perturbations in each case. We find that these contextualized regulatory networks form a spectrum of 13 distinct clusters, with M1 and M2 at the two ends. We demonstrate that a set of three RFs, that is, CEBPB, NFE2L2, and BCL3, is sufficient to change the polarization destination from M1 to M2. siRNA knockdown of the 3-RF-set in THP1-derived M0 cells, despite exposure to an M1 stimulant, significantly attenuated the shift to M1 phenotype and instead increased the expression of M2 markers. The siRNA-mediated knockdown of the 3-RF-set rendered the macrophages hyper-susceptible to Staphylococcus aureus infection, demonstrating the importance of these factors in modulating immune responses. Overall, our results provide insights into the transcriptional mechanisms underlying macrophage polarization and identify key RFs that may be targeted to modulate immune responses.
nc91e72bd2861: Few concepts are as central to evolution as is fitness, and yet the quantification of fitness is often ambiguous. In particular, high-throughput experiments to measure mutant fitness in microbes are increasingly common, but vary widely in their definitions of fitness, which makes their results difficult to compare. Here, we systematize the set of possible fitness statistics according to the following three choices: (1) the encoding of relative abundance (e.g., transforming by a log or logit function), (2) the time scale over which to measure the change in relative abundance, and (3) the choice of a reference subpopulation for calculating relative fitness in bulk competition experiments, such as those using DNA-barcoded mutants. We show that these different choices can lead to significantly different interpretations of mutant fitness in Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Escherichia coli, affecting the magnitude of fitness effects, the apparent presence of epistasis, and even the fitness ranking across mutants. This can confound predictions for evolutionary dynamics and gene functions. Altogether, our results demonstrate the importance of consistent fitness definitions for reproducible results across experiments.
n4ac86288c3e0: In chickens and humans, classical class I molecules of the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) have a spectrum of correlated properties, including cell surface expression and peptide repertoire. However, marked preferences for particular peptide lengths, particular amino acids at the three anchor residues, and particular combinations of amino acids at P2 and Pc-2 as well as at P3 and Pc-3 together lead to high frequencies of major peptides while still allowing the possibility of presenting a wide peptide repertoire. These simplifying principles may eventually allow predictions of pathogen peptides with stable binding for this iconic promiscuous class I molecule, as well as providing the data for more sophisticated peptide prediction methods.
n3520cc9a4d17: Immune privilege, or the capacity of specific tissues to actively limit immune responses, cannot be reduced to passive exclusion. The brain, eye, testis, and placenta each maintain this state through specialized physical barriers, resident immunosuppressive cell populations, and suppression of antigen presentation. Tumor cells metastasizing to these organs co-opt the same molecular programs that immune-privileged tissues evolved to protect themselves, turning biological safeguards into metastatic sanctuaries. The pattern points to selection rather than chance: The cells that thrive are those able to evade specialized immune programs and breach site-specific barriers. Advances in single-cell and spatial profiling, liquid biopsy, and preclinical modeling have now provided the tools to interrogate these ecosystems with previously unavailable resolution. Here, we review the biology of immune-privileged metastatic niches, advances in their detection and molecular profiling, and the therapeutic strategies emerging from this understanding, with an emphasis on molecularly guided treatment over tissue-of-origin classification.
n17e7dea2cfed: Cellular plasticity, a hallmark of normal development, is frequently co-opted by cancers to drive heterogeneity, metastasis, and therapy resistance. Deciphering these dynamic processes requires lineage-tracing technologies capable of recording cellular ancestry. This review outlines the methodological evolution from widely used site-specific recombinase tools to high-resolution, single-cell DNA barcoding. The integration of lineage tracing with single-cell multiomics and spatial transcriptomics now enables the construction of dynamic atlases that link cellular history to molecular state and microenvironment. Key insights reshaping cancer biology include the frequent polyclonal origin of early lesions followed by Darwinian selection toward monoclonal dominance, the revelation that cancer stem cells represent dynamic and plastic states rather than fixed entities, and the identification of specific cellular states critical for metastasis. This synergistic framework provides a powerful means to delineate the rules of tumor evolution, opening new avenues for predicting cell fates and designing strategies to target the roots of malignancy.
n27a0ad5730f1: Companion dogs are increasingly recognized as translational models for studying human physiology and disease. Unlike conventional or genetically engineered laboratory models, dogs are outbred, immunocompetent animals that spontaneously develop complex diseases whose pathogenesis and environmental exposures commonly overlap with those of humans. These distinctive features create opportunities to study mechanisms of disease, progression, and therapeutic responses under conditions that more closely resemble clinical reality. This review highlights evidence for the translational relevance of canine models across multiple therapeutic areas. We further discuss how advances in genomics, transcriptomics, spatial biology, and in vitro and in silico model systems are expanding the translational utility of canine models for applications in human medicine. Although important species differences must be carefully weighed, dogs represent a uniquely valuable comparative model for elucidating disease mechanisms, informing drug development, and accelerating the translation of scientific discoveries to human medicine.
n7d6d098dd517: Unique to mammals, the diaphragm muscle (DIAm) is the major pump muscle for breathing. The DIAm is a skeletal muscle composed of different fiber types with different mechanical and fatigue properties. Thus, by recruiting different MU types, a range of motor behaviors can be accomplished. To support breathing, which is a sustained behavior, fatigue-resistant slow (type I fibers) and fast (type IIa fibers) MUs are recruited. However, the DIAm also subserves short duration, higher-force airway clearance, and voiding behaviors that require recruitment of more fatigable fast (type IIx/IIb) fibers. Importantly, in disease conditions, these fatigable DIAm MUs are more vulnerable, while fatigue-resistant MUs are more resilient.
nadcd13879708: Biophysical pleiotropy, the phenomenon in which a mutation affects multiple protein properties, underlies many genetic diseases and shapes protein evolution, yet remains poorly understood, limiting synthetic biology and therapeutic development. Although extensively studied in soluble proteins, little is known about how pleiotropic effects shaped the evolution of receptor protein functions. Here, we developed a cell-based assay designed to assess pleiotropic effects in G protein–coupled receptors (GPCRs), the largest receptor class in eukaryotes. Because our assay allows for multiple GPCR molecular phenotypes (basal activity, ligand-dependent signaling, and cellular receptor abundance) to be simultaneously assessed, we applied it to study rhodopsin, a visual GPCR that evolved for high phototransduction capabilities by maximizing light-driven responses while minimizing noise. To investigate this, we integrated our assay with deep mutational scanning to test the impacts of ~2,000 single-residue substitutions in rhodopsin across all three molecular phenotypes (~6,000 measurements). By analyzing these data in the context of rhodopsin’s protein structures, we found complex pleiotropic effects that act asymmetrically to impose joint constraints, restricting mutational tolerance in rhodopsin’s retinal binding pocket and G protein interaction interface. A dose–response analysis of rhodopsin signaling revealed that these pleiotropic constraints arise from the dual functions of its chromophore, which acts as an agonist upon light-driven isomerization but also an inverse agonist in darkness. Because these constraints reflect mechanistically driven limitations in the evolution of receptor signaling, these findings reveal a role for biophysical pleiotropy in shaping the signaling capabilities of receptor proteins.
n3551b5ccd0bf: Nitrogen-fixing root nodules develop as lateral organs on legume roots and their formation is restricted by autoregulation of nodulation (AON), a systemic mechanism with unclear evolutionary origins. Because NF-YA4 functions partly redundantly with NF-YA1 to mediate nodule emergence, our results suggest a model in which duplication and neofunctionalization of an ancestral NF-YA-dependent pathway controlling lateral root development facilitated its recruitment to the nodulation program. They also raise the possibility that AON could have evolved, at least in part, through the co-option of a LRR-RK/miR169/ NF-YA regulatory module that limited lateral root development.
n7616a17300ce: Constitutive modeling is fundamental to computational solid mechanics, yet most existing approaches remain material-specific and require retraining or recalibration when materials change. Using hyperelasticity as a testbed, we demonstrate that ICM can be trained once on equilibrium deformation fields spanning diverse materials, geometries, and boundary conditions, enforcing physical equilibrium without stress labels. After training, the same model can be directly deployed on previously unseen hyperelastic materials without retraining. At inference, ICM treats a small set of nonuniform strain fields as physical context to generate constitutive response in a single forward pass. Numerical benchmarks and experimental validation demonstrate accurate stress prediction across out-of-distribution materials and boundary-value problems, together with substantial reductions in deployment cost compared with per-material learning approaches. These results establish in-context learning as a retraining-free paradigm for constitutive modeling, particularly valuable for heterogeneous biological tissues such as the brain, and suggest a pathway toward foundation models for computational mechanics.
nf0c6009ec030: Recently, we lost one of the original developers of the field of molecular electronics. Mark A. Ratner wrote a famous paper in 1974 that developed the theoretical framework for making a molecule act as a rectifier. This idea, and a host of further ideas that were stimulated by this and other papers, led to a huge amount of experimental and theoretical studies that continue to this day. But Mark’s career was much more than that, with leadership at Northwestern University and beyond that continues to shape the scientific enterprise.
n97527331ce2d: Allostery is central to catalysis and regulation, yet how distal perturbations control enzyme activity remains unresolved. We show that a mutational perturbation at the hot spot redistributes the populations of two globally similar conformations with a subtle but critical structural difference that makes one catalytically competent and the other not. Nonequilibrium relaxation simulations further reveal that the transition between these two states in the mutant proceeds through a stepwise sequence of local structural rearrangements rather than a concerted global motion. Guided by this mechanism, we rationally engineer a compensatory second-site mutation that partially restores activity. These results provide a unified thermodynamic and kinetic view of allostery and establish a general, mechanistically guided framework for engineering allosteric regulation in enzymes.
naf6a7c0d4c44: Macromolecular crowding is known to influence the diffusive, binding, kinetic, and equilibrium properties of proteins in a range of environments such as occur inside biological cells or in highly concentrated solutions of protein therapeutics. Here, we present an adaptive model to simulate the association of two solutes in a macromolecularly crowded environment using Brownian dynamics and to compute the corresponding bimolecular association rate constant. The adaptive model represents interactions with atomistic detail for short-range crowder–noncrowder interactions, while using a coarse-grained approach for long-range crowder–noncrowder interactions and all crowder–crowder interactions. This multiscale approach is integrated in the Simulation of Diffusional Association (SDA) software for Brownian dynamics simulation of biomolecular diffusion. We applied this model to compute the rates of association for two contrasting protein-small molecule inhibitor complexes in environments varying in macromolecular crowder type and density, and we used Markov State modeling of the encounter trajectories to analyze the binding pathways. The results reveal competing effects: While the presence of the crowders can hinder ligand binding by reducing the translational diffusion rates of the solutes and obstructing the protein binding sites, crowders can also enhance the bimolecular association rate by other mechanisms, including channeling and the caging effect.
nb9a235fe18d5: Achieving reliable, remote control over multiple stable states in modular systems remains a challenge due to the coupling between modules and history-dependent transitions. Here, we present magnetic origami state machines that enable deterministic navigation from any unknown initial state to any target state under magnetic actuation. By assuming mutually distinct energy barriers in modular Kresling origami assemblies, we realize fully accessible transition graphs with scalable state spaces. Guided by the graph associated to the state machine, a rotating magnetic field induces a universal reset that autonomously drives the system to a known equilibrium state from arbitrary states without sensing or feedback, while pulsed magnetic inputs further enable programmable transitions to any target state via prescribed actuation sequences. A reduced-order Lagrangian mechanics model predicts snap-through dynamics across reset, stepwise programming (between graph nodes), and shortcuts (by adapting pulse magnitude and orientation) where inertia triggers simultaneous multicell transitions with a single pulse. These results establish a general framework for programmable magneto-mechanical state machines with autonomous state reset and full state-space control.
n18015d2920e0: UDP-glucose:glycoprotein glucosyltransferase 1 (UGGT1) plays a central role in quality control of glycoprotein folding within the early secretory pathway, yet the molecular basis of UGGT1 substrate recognition remains poorly understood. This observation supports a mode of binding that places the substrate near the catalytic domain. A dimeric form of UGGT1 was observed in which the glycoprotein substrate binding sites are occluded, suggesting that dimerization may regulate UGGT1 activity. ne341b886c4e1: An opening salvo of lawsuits in US courts has begun holding AI companies accountable through independent doctrinal routes: Product liability and agency law cut as swords, while the shields of Section 230 immunity and First Amendment doctrine begin to crack. This Perspective points out that these converging paths share a unifying principle, built on the very engineering architecture of machine learning (ML) itself. Every ML system, across all variants, is constituted by a human-specified objective function before learning begins. Training data, deployment context, user interaction, and postdeployment oversight add further layers of deliberate human intention traceable to identifiable actors. AI output is therefore not the expression of a single speaker but a composite of layered human intents. It takes a village to raise an AI, and everyone in that village bears a duty of care. This transforms AI accountability from a philosophical puzzle into a tractable legal inquiry: Trace the chain of intentional design decisions across the ML pipeline, grade each actor’s responsibility by their intent’s specificity and foreseeability, and apportion liability accordingly, following the standard three doctrine-neutral questions (attribution, causation, apportionment). Sufficient for most cases, four gaps remain: who owes what share when many hands build one system, proving fault inside an opaque model, harms that surface only after deployment, and remedies that match the technology’s pace. Targeted reforms drawing on environmental, vaccine, and financial regulatory precedents can close these gaps without requiring new legal categories, AI speech rights, AI legal personhood, or defining AI consciousness.
n5ee98e94b56b: The activity of healthy neuronal networks is tightly regulated, and a shift toward hyperexcitability can cause various problems, such as epilepsies, memory deficits, and motor disorders. However, quantifying multiple compensatory mechanisms and their dependence on specific pathophysiological mechanisms has proven challenging, even in computational models. We use simulation-based inference to quantify the interactions of putative compensatory mechanisms in a spiking neuronal network model. Various parameters of the model can compensate for the changes in other parameters to maintain baseline activity, and we estimated their compensatory potential. Furthermore, specific causes of hyperexcitability – interneuron loss, excitatory recurrent synapses, and principal cell depolarization – have distinct compensatory mechanisms that can restore normal excitability. Our results show that spiking neuronal network simulators could generate hypotheses about the mechanisms of pathophysiological network mechanisms.
ncf001944f585: The microstructure of cells within the human cerebral cortex varies across the cortical ribbon, where changes in cytoarchitecture and myeloarchitecture are thought to endow each region of the cortex with its unique function.
